title: EchoStream POC: open-model selection + workload scoping
summary: POC scoping call to agree success criteria, expected workload and timeline for a 4-week open-model POC. Discussed multilingual needs (EN/ES/PT), domain: clinical notes summarization + triage routing. Shortlist: Llama-2 variants, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B, OpenAssistant variants; tradeoffs around latency, quantization, hallucination. Agreed next steps to run benchmarks and provide pricing for hosted vs dedicated runs.
transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya, Connor, Sara (Redwood); Priya, Liam, Omar, Nina (EchoStream)

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm maya from redwood inference, with connor and sara from the solutions team. priya, do you want to kick off with what you want to get out of this call?
[00:12] Dr. Priya: yeah thanks maya. main objective is we want a rapid POC to prove model selection for summarizing clinical encounter notes and an initial triage classifier. must support english and spanish, possibly portuguese later. success criteria are both quality and operational: p95 latency targets, accuracy on our eval set, and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:30] Connor (SE): great. can you give ballpark volume? tokens per doc, concurrent users, and monthly volume?
[00:38] Liam: sure. average encounter note is ~350 tokens, but for summaries we send 512 tokens prepended w/ prompt. expected monthly queries start at 150k, grow to 500k within 6 months. peak concurrency we see during morning shift — estimate 12 to 20 concurrent requests.
[00:56] Sara (SE): okay that helps. batching will matter — do you expect requests to be batchable or strictly low-latency single-shot?
[01:05] Liam: mostly single-shot, but about 40% can be batched (night processing). priority is interactive latency for clinicians.
[01:14] Omar (CTO): and security — we'll need SOC 2 type II evidence, VPC private deployment is a requirement for later stages, and KMS integration. initial POC can be hosted if data is de-identified, but we need private option on the table.
[01:28] Maya: understood. we can do hosted for the POC with a tight NDAs and de-id, then transition to Redwood Private (VPC) for the pilot. we'll include SOC2 docs and architecture notes.
[01:36] Dr. Priya: good. on quality: we have a labeled eval of 2k notes, bilingual. target ROUGE-L for summaries > 0.45 and hallucination rate < 6% measured by our automatic heuristic plus manual spot checks. For triage classifier we need micro-F1 > 0.88.
[01:56] Connor: perfect. for the model shortlist, we propose a set of open-models that balance quality/latency/cost. initial shortlist: Llama-2-70B (quant variants), Mistral-Instruct-7B-v0.1, Falcon-40B, OpenAssistant-13B (finetuned), and a distilled Guanaco variant. we can add a multilingual specialized model if needed.
[02:20] Liam: quick question — we've seen big quality delta between 13B and 70B models on clinical text. are you able to run comparative benchmarks on our eval set?
[02:29] Connor: yes absolutely. plan is to run against your 2k eval with three configuration axes: model variant (70B vs 40B vs 13B/7B), quantization level (fp16 vs q8_0 vs q4), and serving mode (hosted Redwood API vs Redwood Dedicated GPU pool). we'll return p50/p95 latencies, token throughput, and the quality metrics you provided.
[02:52] Maya: to be clear on latency SLOs — you said interactive clinicians expect p95 under 800ms for 512 tokens?
[02:59] Dr. Priya: prefer < 600ms ideally, but we'll accept up to 800ms for the POC if quality is noticeably better.
[03:08] Sara: that's useful. cost tradeoff conversation: big models at low quantization will be higher compute cost; we can show cost per 1M tokens for each config and also show autoscaling/dedicated pricing.
[03:20] Nina (Product): multilingual support — do any of these models have native ES/PT support or will we fallback to translation pipeline?
[03:28] Connor: Mistral and some Falcon derivatives have decent multilingual ability but typically the 70B family models (Llama variants) are stronger. We can measure bilingual performance; if needed we can propose a translation-first flow (translate->summarize->back-translate) for Portuguese, but that's extra latency/cost.
[03:50] Liam: what about hallucination mitigation — you mentioned reranking or grounding?
[03:56] Connor: right — options: 1) prompt engineering + chain of thought constraints, 2) retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a small knowledge base of allowed responses, 3) post-hoc consistency checks + reranker. For POC we recommend lightweight RAG with a small KB for critical fields, to keep hallucinations down. This will affect throughput and latency; we'll measure that in the benchmark.
[04:20] Omar: for the infrastructure, can you explain difference between hosted and dedicated? how fast can dedicated be provisioned for POC?
[04:28] Maya: hosted is immediate — Redwood API with model catalog. Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) takes longer (2-3 weeks typical to provision) but gives predictable latency and data isolation. For the POC we can provision a temporary dedicated node if you want — depends on capacity. We've got burst options too.
[04:44] Dr. Priya: timeline — we'd like results within 4 weeks. Week 1: baseline runs and data alignment; week 2: model shortlist benchmarks; week 3: tuning (quantization, batch config, RAG); week 4: final report and handoff. is that feasible?
[04:59] Connor: yes that's our recommended 4-week cadence. we can start with hosted runs while the dedicated infra is stood up.
[05:07] Liam: what do you need from our side to get started?
[05:11] Maya: deliverables we need: a sanitized sample of 200-500 notes (representative), your eval set (the 2k labeled records), and your latency test harness / expected concurrency profile. Also confirmation on which languages to include for the run.
[05:24] Dr. Priya: we'll share the 2k eval and a 300-sample sanitized pack by tomorrow. we'll redact PHI.
[05:29] Maya: perfect. on benchmarks, we'll run the candidate configs and return a spreadsheet with p50/p95 latencies, cost per 1M tokens, throughput, and quality metrics (ROUGE-L, F1, hallucination rate). we'll also mark recommended config per workload (summaries vs triage).
[05:48] Connor: operationally, expected token accounting: with 150k queries/month at avg 150 tokens output + 512 input = ~100M tokens/month. that will obviously scale to 350M-500M for 500k queries. we'll include cost estimates across that band.
[06:06] Nina: do you support model pinning and canary rollouts? we need a path to production post-POC without rewriting prompts/configs.
[06:15] Sara: yes — Redwood supports model pinning, rollout policies, canary and auto-fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained. we'll include recommended rollout policy in the final report.
[06:26] Omar: any constraints around data residency — our EU clinics need data stored in eu-west for some patients.
[06:33] Maya: we have region routing and can pin requests to eu regions; for POC you'll need to flag those records so we route accordingly. for Private deployments you can fully control residency.
[06:44] Liam: about evaluations — can you run the tests with q8_0 quant and also with fp16 so we can see tradeoffs?
[06:52] Connor: yes. we'll include fp16, q8_0, and q4 runs for the 13/40/70B candidates where supported. some models don't have q4 available; we'll note that.
[07:03] Dr. Priya: curious about inference optimizations — you've mentioned prefix/KV cache earlier, how much does that help for conversational continuity?
[07:11] Connor: KV cache helps more for multi-turn interactions; for single-shot summarization less, but for triage with context it can reduce per-token compute since keys can be cached. we'll capture realistic sequence lengths in the benchmark.
[07:25] Maya: any competitors you evaluated previously?
[07:28] Liam: we've looked at Anthropic, OpenAI hosted, and some vendor-managed Vertex AI flows. we're open to open-models for cost reasons.
[07:39] Sara: we'll include competitor cost baseline for context.
[07:42] [08:00 - brief side conversation about team logistics omitted]
[07:55] Connor: final note on metrics: we'll compute p95 latency for 512 tokens, throughput at 8/16 concurrency, cost per 1M tokens, ROUGE-L, micro-F1 for triage, and an automated hallucination heuristic.
[08:13] Maya: ok, recap and next steps. we'll: 1) run baseline hosted benchmarks across the shortlist; 2) share a detailed spreadsheet with latency/cost/quality; 3) include SOC2 + VPC architecture docs; 4) propose a dedicated node quote if you want reserved capacity.
[08:31] Dr. Priya: timeline and decision criteria — if a model meets ROUGE-L >0.45 and p95 <600ms with hallucination <6% we'll move to a 3-month pilot with dedicated infra.
[08:43] Nina: and pricing signal — send both hosted per-token and a reserved capacity quote so we can model cost at scale.
[08:52] Maya: noted. anything else?
[08:55] Omar: just one ask — add language-specific evals for spanish clinical shorthand, some abbreviations differ.
[09:03] Connor: yes we'll include language-specific breakdowns.
[09:08] Maya: great. thanks everyone. we'll send the benchmark plan and the list of configs by EOD tomorrow, and schedule the first run once we have the sanitized samples.
[09:17] Dr. Priya: thanks all.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts present (model names and acronyms sometimes garbled e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" in one spot).
